title: A build rejected because the TDD predicate is defective, but not proven so, is charged to the item
summary: PR #1079 charges the item for BUILD_DELIVERABLE_REJECTED and leaves a defective predicate to the blocker prover, which ends a proven defect as BLOCKER_ROUTE (console, no charge). Cycle 1761 is the case it misses: its TDD predicate was unsatisfiable (#728), but the lane did not declare a blocker the prover could prove, so the rejection now charges the item. The ceiling bounds the harm: the item is quarantined, not redrawn forever. The predicate defect itself goes unreported to the pipeline.
fix: Before the rejection is coded, run the unsatisfiable-predicate lint (evalqualitycheck.LintUnsatisfiablePredicates) and the protected-path AC check over the cycle's predicates. When either proves a predicate the build could not satisfy, record a pipeline-owned code (not task-level) instead of BUILD_DELIVERABLE_REJECTED.
acceptance: A 1761-shaped workspace whose failing predicate is a proven-unsatisfiable shape classifies as a pipeline failure, not as a charge to the item (red today)
A rejection whose predicates lint clean still charges the item
